author: sascha
name: Change todo priority directly from the collapsed row
description:
Scope: the todo app list UI and its existing record-scoped save flow.

Make the priority displayed on each collapsed todo row an accessible dropdown offering the existing low, normal, high, and urgent values. Selecting a different value should save that task's priority without expanding its full editor. Prevent dropdown mouse and keyboard interaction from triggering the row's fold/unfold action or briefing buttons. Keep the existing full-editor priority control consistent with the saved value, including in grouped views.

Use the current per-record revision checks and automatic local data commits. Preserve unrelated fields, other task drafts, and any unsaved full-editor draft for this task; define reconciliation when that draft also edits priority so a later Save cannot silently undo the quick change or discard other edits. On failure or same-record conflict, show a clear outcome, preserve drafts, and do not leave an unsaved selection looking successfully persisted. Reflect successful changes in priority sorting/filtering without unexpectedly opening the task or losing focus. An unchanged selection should not create a commit.

Acceptance: a collapsed task's priority can be changed with mouse and keyboard; it stays collapsed and persists after reload; grouped and ungrouped views and the full editor agree; unrelated concurrent task edits still succeed; stale same-task edits and network/Git failures are handled visibly without data loss. Check local history for the priority change and test with temporary board data.

Resolve during interaction design: the exact placement/styling, pending-save feedback, and reconciliation of an already-dirty editor. Suggested behavior is to save on selection using the existing save API. No new priority levels or broader list redesign is requested.
